title: Indian Esports Teams Visa Issues: Why Delays Keep Happening
description: Indian esports teams visa issues keep hitting international events, from GodLike and S8UL delays to past rejections, says sportsdigest.in. Here's why.
tags: godlike cod mobile world championship visa

body.text: Indian esports teams visa issues are back in the spotlight. According to sportsdigest.in, Indian squads often qualify for global tournaments, only to run into visa delays, appointment shortages and rejections before they can travel. It matters because a qualification means little if players cannot get to the venue, and the problem has repeatedly affected India's showing on the world stage.
Indian esports teams visa issues: the appointment squeeze
The first hurdle, per the report, is securing a visa appointment early enough. International events run on strict schedules, so teams often have little time to organise travel once they qualify.

Sportsdigest.in points to October 2025, when GodLike Esports and S8UL ran into trouble before the Call of Duty: Mobile World Championship in Poland. GodLike said four of its players had no visas because appointments were unavailable. Three S8UL members faced a similar situation.

The most recent case involves S8UL again. The publication says the team is the only one facing visa delays for the PUBG Mobile Global Championship (PMGC) 2026 in Turkey. Manager Sid has said the process is still ongoing, so the outcome is not yet clear.
Pro players follow the same visa rules as everyone else

Qualifying for a tournament does not give players special access to a country. Sportsdigest.in explains that short-stay visa applications require supporting documents such as the reason for travel and proof of financial arrangements. Officials may also ask for extra paperwork.
That means teams need their invitation letters, tournament confirmations and financial documents in order. Missing or questionable information can slow the process down further.

Esports was officially recognised in India in December 2022 as part of multi-sport events under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. The report stresses that this did not create a separate travel or visa route for professional gamers.

In a July 2024 parliamentary response, the Ministry said no specific policy or guidelines had been framed for esports. The article says this gap can complicate documentation and coordination for players, but it clarifies that the lack of a dedicated regulator is not the reason visas get rejected.
A problem with a long history

items: 2019: Team SouL, TeamIND and Indian Tigers had German visa applications rejected ahead of the PUBG Mobile Club Open in Berlin. They had to compete from India, which sportsdigest.in says hurt them because of network latency.
April 2024: GodLike withdrew from the SPS CODM Masters in Sao Paulo because of delays in Brazilian visas.

body.text: The immediate question is whether S8UL gets its visas in time for PMGC 2026 in Turkey. Beyond that, sportsdigest.in argues that organisers, teams and the authorities need to coordinate better. Early invitations, clear documentation and proper support for travelling players could reduce delays, though the report does not claim any of these will remove the problem entirely.

faqs.q: Why do Indian esports teams face visa problems?
faqs.a: According to sportsdigest.in, the causes include a shortage of visa appointments, tight tournament schedules, documentation requirements and past rejections. No single reason explains every case.

faqs.q: Which Indian esports teams have had visa trouble recently?
faqs.a: Sportsdigest.in reports that GodLike Esports and S8UL faced visa problems before the CODM World Championship in Poland in October 2025. S8UL is also reportedly facing delays ahead of PMGC 2026 in Turkey.

faqs.q: Does esports recognition in India include a visa process for players?
faqs.a: No. Sportsdigest.in notes that esports was recognised in December 2022 as part of multi-sport events, but that did not create a dedicated travel or visa process for professional gamers.
